districts.name: Tijeras Canyon
districts.verbatim_quote: Information on the discovery and production of gold in the Tijeras Canyon district is meager.

districts.name: Mogollon
districts.verbatim_quote: A sergeant named James C. Cooney, who was sta- tioned at Fort Bayard, staked the first claims in the Mogollon (Cooney) district in 1875, but hostile Apache Indians prevented the shipment of ore until 1879.

districts.name: Elizabethtown-Baldy
districts.verbatim_quote: Copper float, found by an Indian on the upper slope of Baldy Peak, was exhibited at Fort Union early in the 1860's (Graton, in Lindgren and others, 1910, p. 92-93).

districts.name: Organ
districts.verbatim_quote: Ore was discovered in the Organ district in 1849 (Dunham, 1935, p. 185-191), and, from the time of discovery to 1952, the district produced copper, lead, silver, zinc, and gold valued at about $2¥2 million (Anderson, 1957, p. 40).

districts.name: Central
districts.verbatim_quote: The Central district, which includes Santa Rita, Hanover, Fierro, and Bayard, is in eastern Grant County and has produced copper, zinc, iron, lead, and small amounts of gold and silver.

districts.name: Pinos Altos
districts.verbatim_quote: The Pinos Altos district is about 8 miles north- east of Silver City in the Pinos Altos Mountains.

districts.name: Steeple Rock
districts.verbatim_quote: The Steeple Rock district is in western Grant County, about 4 miles from the New Mexico-Arizona boundary.

districts.name: Lordsburg
districts.verbatim_quote: The Lordsburg district is 3 to 8 miles south- southwest of the town of Lordsburg at the north end of the Pyramid Mountains.

districts.name: White Oaks
districts.verbatim_quote: The White Oaks district has produced about seven-eighths of the gold in Lincoln County.

districts.name: Nogal
districts.verbatim_quote: The Nogal district, in the Sierra Blanca Range about 6 miles southwest of the town of Nogal, has produced minor amounts of placer and lode gold, mostly before 1908.

districts.name: Jarilla
districts.verbatim_quote: The Jarilla (Orogrande) district is in the Jarilla Mountains about 50 miles north-northeast of El Paso in the southwest corner of Otero County.

districts.name: Cochiti
districts.verbatim_quote: The Cochiti district was prospected in the 1870's or 1880's, but boundary disputes with Mexico damp- ened any early enthusiasm to locate claims.

districts.name: Willow Creek
districts.verbatim_quote: Almost the entire production of the Willow Creek (Pecos) district came from the Pecos mine, formerly known as the Hamilton or Cowles mine.

districts.name: Old Placer
districts.verbatim_quote: The Old Placer (Ortiz, Dolores, Cerrillos) dis- trict is on the east side of the Ortiz Mountains.

districts.name: New Placer
districts.verbatim_quote: The New Placer (San Pedro) district is on the west side of the San Pedro Mountains between the towns of San Pedro and Golden.

districts.name: Hillsboro
districts.verbatim_quote: The Hillsboro (Las Animas) district is about 25 miles southwest of Truth Or Consequences.

districts.name: Rosedale
districts.verbatim_quote: The Rosedale district is in the northern San Mateo Mountains in the southwest corner of So- corro County, about 25 miles southwest of Mag- dalena.

source.citation: Koschmann, A. H., and Bergendahl, M. H., 1968, Principal Gold-Producing Districts of the United States: U.S. Geological Survey Professional Paper 610, 283 p.
source.title: Principal Gold-Producing Districts of the United States
